summary: The change is correct, keeps every key in the window, and runs one sliding-only change with full layers as an in-run control, so a single run is readable from the per-kernel profile. The likely result is a small gain or flat: FA3's main loop and its host split heuristic probably already bound local attention by the window, so the realistic win is limited to a smaller combine/split schedule, minus the extra trim launch.
justification: Correctness holds. FA3 aligns causal masking to the bottom-right, so query j at local position len_win-L+j keeps the same relative window. RoPE is already applied before FA3, so absolute positions are not needed. first_page*P <= first_tok <= len-W keeps every window key inside the trimmed table. At page_size 64, len_win <= W+63 needs ceil((W+63)/64) <= ceil(W/64)+1 pages, which NP provides. Short contexts give first_page=0 and the same table as today. On the mechanism, the profile limits the upside. Sliding FA3 main time is 13.2 us at decode_32 for about 16.8 MB of window KV. That is about 1.3 TB/s, the page-size-1 gather rate LESSONS reports for full layers, which suggests the main kernel already iterates only window blocks (FA3's n_block_min/max are window-bounded per tile). The host get_num_splits also uses a window-clamped seqlen_k_loaded when is_local. So the only plausible lever is the device-side dynamic-split path: prepare_varlen_num_blocks_kernel (1.8 us) plus FlashAttnFwdCombine (2.5-4.1 us on every sliding shape). If prepare sizes per-batch splits from the full ~80K seqlen_k rather than the window, most splits are empty and combine reduces over too many partials, and trimming fixes that. If prepare already honours the window, this is flat minus one launch. The prepare kernel itself will not get cheaper: it is one launch of B threads whatever the table width, so the hypothesis's claim that the prepare kernel's work shrinks is wrong, and it stays in the graph because scheduler_metadata is None on sliding. Expected magnitudes are optimistic. The 'FA3 spends ~8-10 us' figure understates the 13.2 us main kernel but overstates what can move: at best about 1-3 us of combine per sliding shape against a ~2 us + ~0.3 us node trim launch. The batch-16/32 'faster' expectations are therefore plausible but small (low single digits per shape), and decode_1/verify_1 may lose by the launch. Sliding shapes carry weight 46 against 16 for full, so even 1-2 us per sliding shape moves the geomean by about 1-3%, near the ~1.5% drift. Weakest link: whether FA3's dynamic-split prepare already clamps per-batch n_blocks to the local window. The hypothesis says so itself and does not resolve it from FA3 source.
confounders: fused-preattention-triton: no confound. It writes the new k/v rows and q before FA3, and the trim kernel reads only cache_seqlens and page_table (inputs). Their order on the stream is fixed and the cache contents are the same either way. Its own time (_pre_attention_kernel row) is separate in the profile.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing: no confound. It is gated on window == 0, so sliding layers never take the paired path. Full-layer rows double as this run's drift control (they should be flat within ~1.5-2.5%). The in-flight paired-heads-launch-cleanup runs touch only the full path and will not land on this branch's base.
interference: No companion is warranted. The change has one effect (what FA3 sees on sliding layers) plus one cost (the trim launch), and the profile separates the two without another run. A gain shows as a smaller FlashAttnFwdCombine and/or main-kernel row on sliding shapes. A loss with unchanged FA3/combine/prepare rows is the trim launch alone, and the hypothesis then goes to do-not-retry together with fa3-num-splits-sliding (already held). Neither landed hypothesis touches the sliding FA3 call, and sliding-single-launch-fused-attention regressed and did not land, so no ab-revert or ab-tune can change how this result reads. When harvesting, read the per-shape rows and the combine/prepare/main kernel times, not the headline, because the expected effect is near the drift floor. If FA3 does shrink but the launch eats the gain, the follow-up is to fold the trim into _pre_attention_kernel's grid (B extra programs) as a separate hypothesis, not a companion now.
rules_flags: No violation found. The attended set is the whole 2,048-token window per query (FA3's window mask is unchanged; the trim only drops pages outside every query's window), so this is not block-skipping or sparse attention.

pt_win/len_win are fixed-shape allocations each call (shape depends only on config: B, window, L, page_size), computed on the device from the input cache_seqlens. There is no .item(), no max over inputs on the host, and nothing cached across calls. This is graph-safe.

Implementation must-dos: compute NP and the grid from config only (never page_table contents); keep the -1 masking for reads past page_table.size(1); pass pt_win as contiguous int32 (FA3 requires a page_table stride of 1 in the last dim).
open_questions: Does FA3 (the sgl_kernel build at this commit) clamp per-batch n_blocks to the local window in prepare_varlen_num_blocks / the dynamic split count? Reading flash_prepare_scheduler.cu would predict the result before spending a check. If it clamps, expect flat-minus-launch.

Does the combine kernel's cost scale with the number of splits FA3 picks, or is it ~2.5-4 us fixed launch+latency? If fixed, only a 1-split schedule (fa3-single-split-sliding) removes it, and trimming helps only insofar as it makes FA3 choose num_splits=1.

Order relative to fa3-single-split-sliding (queued p4): both target the same combine/split overhead. Run this one first. If FA3's split count does not drop, single-split is the remaining probe of the same lever. If it does drop, single-split becomes largely redundant.
